global_decisions.decision: Self-hosted Fixer MCP is fully user-operated and costs exactly $0; payment is never required to run it.
The Fixer subscription is optional and pays for managed value or entitlements, not access to free self-hosting.
A creator, then the activated project governance body, decides whether a project joins Fixer Exchange; settlement fees are enforced after opt-in.
The Exchange fee rate remains an Architect/legal/unit-economics decision; the former 0% take-rate rule is superseded.
All model and infrastructure consumption, including BYOK, routes through a Fixer gateway for policy, accounting, and budget enforcement.
R1 is an end-to-end system whose shipped surfaces are explicitly labelled stable, alpha, or experimental.
Every real crypto action requires an explicit operator signature, exact recipient and amount preview, and a hard spend cap.
Current Fixer Studio is the canonical cockpit; the retired App Server cockpit must not be revived.
A new Rust terminal is required, with the Python launcher retained until migration acceptance passes.
Economic votes may be unit-weighted, while constitution, mission, publicity, and ownership changes need an additional community protection threshold.

architect_gates.title: MCP binary restart and build-epoch confirmation
architect_gates.trigger: A reviewed control-plane change requires a new Fixer MCP binary.
architect_gates.required_action: Restart Fixer MCP and explicitly confirm the exact required build from a fresh process.
architect_gates.blocking_scope: All later wave creation, launch, deferred release, repair, retry, and acceptance dispatch.
architect_gates.evidence_requirement: Durable required/running build IDs and epochs, distinct process identities, restart confirmation, and explicit orchestration resume.

architect_gates.title: Real-wallet funding and signature
architect_gates.trigger: The controlled real-SOL transaction is ready with a validated preview and test wallet.
architect_gates.required_action: Fund the test wallet if needed and sign the exact transaction explicitly.
architect_gates.blocking_scope: Broadcast of any real crypto transaction.
architect_gates.evidence_requirement: Recipient, amount, fees, hard cap, simulation result, explicit signature, transaction ID, and reconciliation record.

architect_gates.title: Exchange settlement fee
architect_gates.trigger: Exchange settlement implementation needs a concrete fee schedule.
architect_gates.required_action: Approve fee rate and minimum only after unit-economics and legal review.
architect_gates.blocking_scope: Production Exchange settlement and public fee claims.
architect_gates.evidence_requirement: Approved fee schedule, versioned policy, legal review, and enforcement tests.

architect_gates.title: Payment rails and commercial terms
architect_gates.trigger: A payment or managed-provider integration is ready to leave sandbox/research.
architect_gates.required_action: Approve the legally available operating entity, merchant path, refund rules, and provider commercial terms.
architect_gates.blocking_scope: Production charges, recurring billing, and resale of managed model usage.
architect_gates.evidence_requirement: Current primary-source terms, legal/tax findings, sandbox reconciliation, and signed provider/merchant account decision.

architect_gates.title: Compute contracting and geography
architect_gates.trigger: Fixer is ready to resell or coordinate third-party or contributed compute.
architect_gates.required_action: Choose direct-customer versus reseller/MoR structure and approve geographic restrictions.
architect_gates.blocking_scope: Production paid compute and cross-border contributed-resource scheduling.
architect_gates.evidence_requirement: Provider contracts, sanctions/residency analysis, abuse model, and explicit operator contribution consent.

architect_gates.title: Public-project legal wrapper
architect_gates.trigger: On-chain/project units are ready to represent enforceable economic or ownership rights.
architect_gates.required_action: Approve a legal wrapper and the boundary between on-chain rules and off-chain assets/IP.
architect_gates.blocking_scope: Claims that units are equity, ownership, or legally enforceable revenue rights.
architect_gates.evidence_requirement: Jurisdiction-specific legal review, constitution text, risk disclosures, and accepted governance tests.

architect_gates.title: Product name and brand
architect_gates.trigger: The combined landing and production surfaces are ready for public launch.
architect_gates.required_action: Approve product name, logo, palette, and positioning.
architect_gates.blocking_scope: Final branded launch assets and broad public campaign.
architect_gates.evidence_requirement: Approved brand system and checked desktop, web, manager, and agent-readable applications.

features.title: Wave Engine v2 core lifecycle
features.summary: Project-scoped recursive and batched waves with explicit phase, gate, control, failure governance, acceptance, immutable outcomes, and build-epoch restart fencing.
decisions: Null/zero child depth disables recursion and positive depth decrements through an acyclic root lineage.
Batch launch/wait is project-scoped and additive to the single-wave API.
Failure decisions are backend-enforced; a strict majority pauses and one eligible isolated failure gets at most one governed repair.
Acceptance is distinct from implementation review.
A required build epoch fences dispatch until a fresh matching process confirms it.

evidence.note: Current lifecycle, failure, acceptance, and restart contract.
Lineage, failure policy, transition, and build-state implementation.
Project-scoped additive batch wrappers.
State, failure, acceptance, and restart coverage.
Reviewed base includes final linearizable restart hardening.

acceptance_criteria: Validate root lineage, depth, descendant-wave and session ceilings transactionally.
Preserve single-wave behavior while isolating batch item failures.
Block reviewer, repair, retry, acceptance, and child dispatch under paused failure policy.
Keep implementation review and acceptance separately queryable.
Compare required/running epochs, build IDs, and distinct process identities without stale downgrade.
Keep terminal outcomes inspectable after cleanup.
